scope: Actual Server API runtime, common checkpoints and recovery against disposable PostgreSQL; no provider acceptance or production adoption claimed.

checks: fresh installation includes additive API migration once
two executors race: only one durable attempt can start
a second module instance cannot reconcile a live physical executor
concurrent exchanges spend exactly the persisted HTTP dispatch budget
initial arm is not charged twice and failed over-budget exchange is rolled back
completed HTTP proof separates local closure from native process claims
qualification cannot replace original content or a returned nonce after completion
common checkpoint accepts API proof and ACK is idempotent
forged closure cannot acknowledge a proof
rollback refuses to discard recovery metadata after API dispatch
armed-before-start crash produces a closed unknown tombstone without dispatch/replay
a stale worker cannot dispatch after reconciliation has fenced its job
common administrative reconciliation closes the unknown run and releases its SQL slot
failed terminal SQL rolls back its physical row without inventing a durable proof
only the same executor with attested completed local work can recover failed terminal persistence
positive local closure recovery retains payload binding and never replays a request
completed response with failed SQL persistence settles through common recovery without another generation
HTTP cannot start from claimed phase before durable arming
no provider or HTTP requests were attempted during SQL verification

execution_history.finding: Raw TypeORM UPDATE RETURNING returned [rows,affectedCount]; checking array length===1 rejected legitimate additional exchange reservations.
execution_history.resolution: Root changed the budget reservation to WITH changed AS(UPDATE...RETURNING) SELECT id FROM changed, preserving atomic limit/fence checks.
Same Root CTE fix; neither failure contacted any provider.

execution_history.finding: Test directly reconciled API metadata but omitted common recovery/reconciliation, leaving an unknown run occupying owner admission; next seed could not claim. The production budget fix had passed before this assertion.
execution_history.resolution: Test uses actual RecoverNodiaAiJobs/ReconcileNodiaAiRuntime/Cleanup and ReleaseNodiaAiRuntimeSlot, including administrator actor, instead of bypassing admission.

execution_history.wall_time_scope: Reported tool command wall time including SSH; not SQL latency or isolated Node duration.

safety_and_cost.network_boundary: global fetch replaced by a throwing guard for the entire test; actual invocation count0
safety_and_cost.cleanup: Finally closes the fixture DataSource and removes only its random template_ai92 owned Docker container with --volumes; no prune or shared volume action. Successful test exit requires cleanup completion.

limits: No actual provider, key, model or modality was qualified by SQL fixtures.
Tests of owner-live denial and positive local closure run in the same process; SIGKILL/PID-reuse/reboot rules also have separate owner unit tests, not physical crash acceptance here.
A completed local HTTP executor with failed SQL persistence retains its known result binding; this does not prove remote cancellation.
Original failed reports remain failed and their private stderr is not included.
No application API/worker/Native restart, production migration, deploy or adoption was performed by this test.
